abstract: Smaller social networks (SNs) negatively influence cognition, psychiatric trajectories and mortality. Studies linking SNs to resting-state functional connectivity (FC) inconsistently suggest orbito-frontal and frontoparietal regions and implicate a potential role for empathy and sex. We investigate how SN characteristics relate to FC, additionally assessing if empathy and sex alter these associations. Group-independent component analysis was applied to multi-band resting-state fMRI from 83 participants (Caltech Conte dataset: ds003798). The Social Network Index measures SN-contacts (SN-contacts) SN-diversity (number of roles) and SN-embeddedness (number of contact groups) and the Empathy Quotient measured empathy. Using MANCOVA, we investigate if resting-state network power and connectivity are associated with SNI measures and whether these relationships differ by empathizing ability and sex. Participants aged 18-48 (mean age 29.3+/-7.0, 55% male) demonstrated SN-contacts and SN-diversity associated with lower frontal-pole FC within the default-mode network (DMN, q-values<0.05). Empathy altered how SN-diversity and SN-contacts relate to superior lateral-occipital, default mode and salience network FC (q-values<0.05). Finally, males and females showed diverging associations of SN-contacts and SN-diversity with salience network power. Smaller SNs were associated with increased anterior-DMN FC, potentially indicating a tendency towards internally-directed cognition in more socially isolated individuals. Opposing relationships between SNs with salience and lateral-frontoparietal networks by empathy level highlights empathy as critical for understanding social biology. Males and females differed in SN associations with salience network coherency, supporting known sex-specific neural correlates of social behavior. These findings provide insights into the biology of social networks, offering potential targets for studying social deficits in psychiatric populations.

summary: Study of 83 adults linking social network size, diversity and embeddedness to resting-state brain connectivity, with empathy and sex modulating effects.
title: Social Connection: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Associations with Social Networks, and the Roles of Empathy and Sex
